question.text: The residents of a particular locality were administered a particular medicine of a company continuously for three months. The locality which had reported high incidence of Hepatitis B before the administration of the medicine reported no cases at the end of this period. The company claimed that this was because their medicine helped the residents develop immunity against Hepatitis B. Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the claim of the company?

options.label: A
options.text: A few cases of Hepatitis B were reported in the locality a month after the company started administering the medicine to the residents.

options.label: B
options.text: The incidence of Hepatitis B is found to be very high during winter, which lasts for about four months in the region, and winter set in three months back.

options.label: C
options.text: Research shows that any medicine capable of helping develop immunity against Hepatitis B takes about six months to show results.

options.label: D
options.text: Usually newborn children are more affected by Hepatitis B, and there were no children born in the locality in the past three months.

answer.correctText: Research shows that any medicine capable of helping develop immunity against Hepatitis B takes about six months to show results.

question.text: Ms. E, a serious protagonist of environmental protection, wins a mayoral election to city ‘C’ against Mr. D. The success of Ms. E, against Mr. D in the election could be attributed to her concern for the environment in all of the following cases EXCEPT when

options.label: A

answer.correctText: Mr. D is a champion of environmental protection.

question.text: The life expectancy of the population of a country has increased from forty five (twenty five years ago) to seventy now—due to increased medical facilities and better health consciousness in people. However, an insurance company in the country has not lowered the premium substantially despite the life expectancy going up. Which of the following, if true, would rationalize the action of the insurance company in not lowering the insurance premium?

options.label: A
options.text: The increase in life expectancy has been significant only in the past five years.

options.label: B
options.text: There have been fewer deaths due to cancer in recent years, whereas twenty five years back it was claiming a number of lives.

options.label: C
options.text: The average age of the population of the country remained at around forty five only due to the increased birth rate in the past twenty five years.

options.label: D
options.text: The country had been at war with all its neighbours during the past twenty five years, resulting in heavy casualties among its soldiers.

answer.correctText: The country had been at war with all its neighbours during the past twenty five years, resulting in heavy casualties among its soldiers.

question.text: A company found that the attrition rate among its employees, especially among the skilled, has been particularly high in the last three months. As the company had introduced night shifts three months ago, it was concluded that this was the reason for the attrition. The employees working in night shifts were, therefore paid per cent extra wages. Which of the following would strongly support the above conclusion?

options.label: A
options.text: The wages of the employees compared to those of employees in other companies of comparable size in the same locality are 25% higher.

options.label: B
options.text: The productivity of employees working in the night shift is higher.

options.label: C
options.text: The number of night shift employees is less than that of the day shift employees.

options.label: D
options.text: The attrition rate is higher in the case of night shift employees.

answer.correctText: The attrition rate is higher in the case of night shift employees.
